# South West Emergency Evacuation Procedure

Document family: `family.fire.south-west-evacuation`
Version: 1.0
Applies to: South West Region and descendant services
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

## Alarm response

On discovering fire or smoke, activate the nearest call point, call 999 and begin
the service's progressive evacuation plan. Staff must not delay evacuation to
collect personal belongings or records.

## Regional fallback assembly arrangement

Unless an approved site procedure names a different location, South West staff and visitors assemble at the signed front visitor car park.
The senior person
present takes the attendance folder and reports missing people to the fire and
rescue service.

## Applicability

This procedure applies to every Alderbridge service in the South West Region,
including Harbour View in Bristol and Meadow Court in Exeter. A site-specific
procedure may contain additional local facts, such as a different assembly point,
that must also be surfaced when answering a site-specific query.

# Harbour View Fire Evacuation Procedure

Document family: `family.fire.harbour-view-evacuation`
Version: 1.0
Applies to: Harbour View only
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

## Local building arrangement

Harbour View is divided into three fire compartments. Staff initially move each
person beyond the nearest fire-resisting doors and continue evacuation only when
the incident requires it.

## Harbour View assembly point

At Harbour View, staff and visitors assemble in the east garden beyond the laundry gate, not in the front visitor car park.
The nurse in charge takes the
red emergency folder from reception and meets the fire and rescue service at the
main entrance.

## Relationship to the regional procedure

The South West regional procedure remains applicable to Harbour View. This
site-specific procedure supplies the local assembly point and building facts;
it does not make the regional alarm and emergency-call duties irrelevant.

## Arrival and identity

All visitors must sign in at reception and wear the issued visitor badge.
A contractor must additionally show photographic identification and be met by the
employee responsible for the work.

## Fire information

Reception staff tell visitors how to recognise the fire alarm and direct them to
the assembly arrangement for that location.
Visitors must not use lifts during an evacuation and must remain with their host or follow staff instructions.

## Confidentiality and infection precautions

Visitors must not photograph records, staff or people supported without explicit
authorisation. They must follow any displayed infection-control precautions and
postpone non-essential visits when they have symptoms of a transmissible illness.

## Departure

Visitors sign out, return their badge and notify reception if their host is no
longer available. The sign-in record is used during emergency roll calls.

# Outbreak Visiting Restrictions Procedure

Document family: `family.visitors.outbreak-restrictions`

During a declared outbreak, each resident may continue to receive one nominated essential visitor unless an individual risk assessment identifies a specific reason to pause that visit. End-of-life visiting is supported with proportionate infection-control measures.

The manager reviews restrictions every forty-eight hours with infection-control advice. Blanket suspension of all visits is not the default response.

Document family: `family.health-safety.lone-working`
Version: 1.0

Managers assess travel, location, task, communication, known behaviour and emergency-access risks before lone work is allocated. Controls may include scheduled welfare calls, paired visits, personal alarms or a decision that the task cannot be completed alone.

If a welfare check is missed, the separate welfare-check procedure governs escalation. Staff must not treat a mobile phone signal as the only control where coverage is unreliable.

# Missing Person Procedure

Document family: `family.safeguarding.missing-person`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 July 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

When a person cannot be located, staff check the agreed immediate search areas without delaying emergency escalation. The shift leader reviews the person's missing-person profile, known risks, likely destinations, communication needs and recent events. Police must be contacted immediately where the person's risk plan requires it or there is reason to believe they face imminent harm.

Staff record the last confirmed sighting, clothing, mobility, medicines, search actions and notifications. On return, the person is welcomed and offered support before a proportionate review. Staff must not use punitive restrictions as a response to the incident.

Spills are guarded and cleaned immediately using the appropriate method. Warning signs are a temporary control and must be removed when the floor is dry. Damaged flooring, poor lighting and trailing cables are reported and isolated where they create immediate risk.

After a fall, staff protect the person, obtain clinical assessment as required and avoid moving them unless remaining in place creates greater danger. The incident record and the person's falls plan are reviewed separately.

## Immediate protection

If anyone is in immediate danger, staff must call the emergency services and
take proportionate steps to reduce further harm. Evidence must be preserved;
staff should not confront an alleged perpetrator or conduct their own interview.

## Reporting

Every safeguarding concern must be reported to the shift leader or registered manager immediately and recorded before the staff member finishes the shift.
The registered manager decides whether to notify the local authority safeguarding
team, but a manager's absence must never delay immediate protective action.

## Speaking up

Staff may report directly to the safeguarding lead when the concern involves
their manager. No employee will be disadvantaged for raising a genuine concern
in good faith.

# Safe Administration of Medicines Policy

Document family: `family.medication.administration`
Version: 2.0
Effective: 1 May 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

## Purpose and scope

This policy applies to all Alderbridge services and establishes the minimum
controls for receiving, preparing, administering and recording medicines. It
does not replace a person's prescription, care plan or PRN protocol. Staff must
work within their assessed competence and seek clinical advice whenever the
record, label and current instructions do not agree.

## Authorisation to administer

Only staff with current medicines training and a recorded competency assessment
may administer medicines without direct supervision. Agency staff must also
complete the local medicines orientation before their first medicines round.
The shift leader checks the allocation at the start of every shift.

## Seven checks

Immediately before administration, the member of staff must confirm the right person, medicine, dose, route, time, reason and documentation.
Identity must be
checked against the MAR and the person's agreed identifier; room number alone
is not an identifier. The medicine label must be legible, in date and consistent
with the current MAR instruction.

## Recording administration

The member of staff must sign the Medication Administration Record (MAR) immediately after observing that the person has taken the dose.
Staff must not pre-sign a MAR.
If the medicine is not given, the correct exception code and a contemporaneous note are required.

| Circumstance | MAR code | Immediate action |
|---|---|---|
| Person refuses | R | Record the reason offered and follow the care-plan escalation |
| Medicine unavailable | U | Inform the shift leader and arrange an urgent supply check |
| Clinical instruction to omit | O | Record the prescriber's name and instruction |
| Person away from service | A | Confirm the absence in the daily record |

## Missed, delayed or refused doses

# Medication Error Reporting Form

| Medicine unavailable | U | Inform the shift leader and arrange an urgent supply check |
| Clinical instruction to omit | O | Record the prescriber's name and instruction |
| Person away from service | A | Confirm the absence in the daily record |

## Missed, delayed or refused doses

Staff must not give a delayed dose until they have checked the medicine-specific
window or obtained clinical advice. A refused dose must be handled without
coercion. The shift leader must be informed before the end of the medicines
round, and urgent clinical advice is required where the medicine is time
critical or the care plan identifies a material risk.

## PRN medicines

PRN means medicine given when required. Before a PRN dose, staff must consult
the current protocol for indication, minimum interval and maximum daily dose.
The reason for administration and the observed outcome must be recorded. A PRN
medicine must not be offered merely because it appears on the MAR.

## Storage checks

Before administering a refrigerated medicine, staff must confirm that the
latest temperature record is within 2°C to 8°C.
If it is outside that range, the medicine must be quarantined and the medicines storage procedure followed; staff must not decide independently that the medicine remains usable.

## Controlled drugs

Where the controlled-drugs procedure requires a witness, both staff members
must complete the register at the time of administration. A later countersignature
does not satisfy the witness requirement.

## Incident escalation and audit

An unexplained MAR gap, incorrect dose, wrong person, wrong medicine or omitted
time-critical dose is a medication incident. Staff must first protect the person,
obtain clinical advice where needed, inform the shift leader and complete the
medication incident record. The registered manager arranges a monthly audit of
MAR records, stock balances and recurring exception codes.

## Preparation and interruption control

The administering worker prepares medicines for one person at a time and keeps the MAR available throughout the round. Medicines are not pre-poured for several people to save time. If preparation is interrupted before identity or medicine checks are complete, the worker returns to the beginning of the checking sequence.

# Controlled Drugs Procedure

Document family: `family.medication.controlled-drugs`
Version: 2.0
Effective: 1 July 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

An authorised staff member and an independent authorised witness must observe each controlled-drug administration. Both sign the register at the time of administration; a later countersignature is prohibited. The running balance is checked against physical stock after every entry.

A discrepancy must be escalated immediately, not at the end of the shift. The shift leader secures the cabinet, repeats the balance with a second witness and informs the registered manager. Where diversion or harm is suspected, safeguarding and incident-reporting procedures also apply.

Returned or expired controlled drugs are stored in the designated segregated section until pharmacy collection. Destruction requires the authorised witness and a contemporaneous register entry.

# Hand Hygiene Procedure

Document family: `family.infection.hand-hygiene`
Version: 2.0
Effective: 1 April 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Use liquid soap and water when hands are visibly dirty, after caring for a person with vomiting or diarrhoea, and whenever spore-forming infection is suspected. Alcohol hand rub is suitable for routine decontamination only when hands are visibly clean and the organism is not one for which soap and water is required.

Staff clean all hand surfaces for at least 20 seconds, dry thoroughly and keep wrists free of watches during direct care.

# PRN Medicines Protocol

Document family: `family.medication.prn`
Version: 1.0
Effective: 1 March 2025
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

PRN means medicine prescribed to be given when required. Before offering a PRN medicine, staff must check the person's current protocol for the indication, minimum interval, maximum dose in 24 hours and non-medicine measures to try first. A PRN entry on the MAR is not, by itself, enough information to administer safely.

Staff record the reason for the dose, time, quantity and observed outcome. If the medicine is ineffective, requested unusually often or refused when symptoms remain concerning, the shift leader must review the care plan and obtain clinical advice. PRN medicine must never be used for staff convenience or as an unrecorded response to distress.

An unexplained MAR gap, incorrect dose, wrong person, wrong medicine or omitted

does not replace a person's prescription, care plan or PRN protocol. Staff must
work within their assessed competence and seek clinical advice whenever the

## Authorisation to administer

may administer medicines without direct supervision. Agency staff must also

## Seven checks

Immediately before administration, the member of staff must confirm the right person, medicine, dose, route, time, reason and documentation.
Identity must be
checked against the MAR and the person's agreed identifier; room number alone
is not an identifier. The medicine label must be legible, in date and consistent
with the current MAR instruction.

## Recording administration

The member of staff must sign the Medication Administration Record (MAR) immediately after observing that the person has taken the dose.
Staff must not pre-sign a MAR.
If the medicine is not given, the correct exception code and a contemporaneous note are required.

| Circumstance | MAR code | Immediate action |
|---|---|---|
| Person refuses | R | Record the reason offered and follow the care-plan escalation |
| Medicine unavailable | U | Inform the shift leader and arrange an urgent supply check |
| Clinical instruction to omit | O | Record the prescriber's name and instruction |
| Person away from service | A | Confirm the absence in the daily record |

## Missed, delayed or refused doses

Staff must not give a delayed dose until they have checked the medicine-specific
window or obtained clinical advice. A refused dose must be handled without
coercion. The shift leader must be informed before the end of the medicines
round, and urgent clinical advice is required where the medicine is time
critical or the care plan identifies a material risk.

## PRN medicines

PRN means medicine given when required. Before a PRN dose, staff must consult
the current protocol for indication, minimum interval and maximum daily dose.
The reason for administration and the observed outcome must be recorded. A PRN
medicine must not be offered merely because it appears on the MAR.

## Storage checks

Before administering a refrigerated medicine, staff must confirm that the
latest temperature record is within 2°C to 8°C.
If it is outside that range, the medicine must be quarantined and the medicines storage procedure followed; staff must not decide independently that the medicine remains usable.

## Controlled drugs

Where the controlled-drugs procedure requires a witness, both staff members
must complete the register at the time of administration. A later countersignature
does not satisfy the witness requirement.

## Incident escalation and audit

An unexplained MAR gap, incorrect dose, wrong person, wrong medicine or omitted
time-critical dose is a medication incident. Staff must first protect the person,
obtain clinical advice where needed, inform the shift leader and complete the
medication incident record. The registered manager arranges a monthly audit of
MAR records, stock balances and recurring exception codes.

## Preparation and interruption control

The administering worker prepares medicines for one person at a time and keeps the MAR available throughout the round. Medicines are not pre-poured for several people to save time. If preparation is interrupted before identity or medicine checks are complete, the worker returns to the beginning of the checking sequence.

A medicine change is accepted only from an authorised prescriber or through the approved clinical communication route. Where a prescription or care plan requires observations, the worker confirms the current result before administration and records it in the designated place. A result copied from an earlier shift is not a current observation. Values outside the stated parameters are escalated before the medicine is given.

Staff seek emergency help for severe breathing difficulty, collapse or another life-threatening reaction, then follow internal reporting. Less urgent concerns are reported promptly to the prescriber or clinical service and documented with onset, observations and action taken.

## End-of-round reconciliation

At the end of the round, the administering worker checks that every due MAR entry has an administration code, a documented reason for omission or an active escalation. Unexplained blank boxes are resolved before handover. The trolley, refrigerator and controlled-drug storage are secured, and any stock discrepancy is escalated under the relevant procedure.

Staff record the reason for the dose, time, quantity and observed outcome. # Data Protection Policy

Document family: `family.gdpr.data-protection`
Version: 2.0
Effective: 1 January 2026
Synthetic engineering benchmark material

Personal information must be collected for a defined purpose, limited to what is necessary, kept accurate and retained only as long as required. Staff must lock paper records away and use approved systems for electronic records.

Suspected loss, misdirection or unauthorised disclosure must be reported through the privacy incident channel immediately and no later than four hours after discovery. Staff must not investigate by accessing another person's account.

## Responsibilities and lawful handling

Every employee is responsible for the information they create, receive and share. Managers design local processes so staff can meet this policy during normal work rather than relying on memory or informal workarounds. The Data Protection Officer advises on lawful basis, data-rights requests, high-risk processing and reportable breaches but does not take ownership away from operational teams.

Access is granted according to role and current need. A colleague's ability to open a record does not establish a legitimate reason to view it. Shared accounts are prohibited. Staff lock screens when leaving a device, keep authentication factors private and report unexpected access prompts to IT Security.

Special-category information about health, disability, ethnicity, beliefs, sexuality or trade-union membership requires additional care. It is recorded only where relevant to care, employment or another defined lawful purpose. Curiosity, convenience and a desire to build a “complete file” are not purposes.

## Sharing and communication

Before sharing personal information, staff confirm the recipient, purpose, minimum necessary content and secure channel. Email address auto-complete must be checked before sending. Large distributions use an approved mailing tool or blind-copy arrangement where recipients should not see one another.
